title: MGFRec: Towards Reinforced Reasoning Recommendation with Multiple Groundings and Feedback

problem.claim: Reasoning-based recommendation requires reasoning about user interests and generating recommended items.

gap.claim: Previous methods typically reasoned only in language space, which could lead to over-interpreting user interests and deviating from real items.

contributions.claim: The authors propose multiple rounds of grounding during inference to help an LLM understand the actual item space and keep reasoning aligned with real items.
The authors introduce a user agent that provides feedback during each grounding step so the LLM can recognize and adapt to user interests.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report comprehensive experiments on three Amazon review datasets.
The authors report that incorporating multiple groundings and feedback is effective.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs have motivated reasoning-based recommendation because of their reasoning and generation capabilities.
Prior methods generally remained within language space and could diverge from actual items.
The proposed approach uses multiple grounding rounds and user-agent feedback during inference.
Experiments on three Amazon review datasets are reported to demonstrate effectiveness.
The findings emphasize reasoning within the actual item space for recommendation.

source_observation.claim: Reasoning confined to language space can over-interpret interests and deviate from real items.

interpretation.claim: Recommendation reasoning may benefit from explicit interaction with the domain's item space.

application.claim: Use repeated grounding steps that connect generated reasoning to available items.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the evaluated recommendation setting or datasets.

source_observation.claim: Feedback is provided during each grounding step to help adapt to user interests.

interpretation.claim: Iterative user feedback may improve alignment between reasoning and user preferences.

application.claim: Incorporate user-agent feedback into iterative grounding workflows.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the feedback mechanism, user-agent implementation, or conditions under which feedback improves outcomes.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the grounding mechanism or inference procedure.
The abstract does not identify the three Amazon review datasets or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not quantify effectiveness or compare results with specific baselines.
The abstract does not describe the user agent's feedback protocol.
